messages:
alex_platform: :rotating_light: noticed spike in 5xx and GPU OOMs in ap-southeast-1 around 1932104400. Autoscaler exhausted reserved capacity; tried a weighted DNS failover to us-east but telemetry shows many clients still resolving to ap-southeast IPs.

maria_netops: what TTLs were on the A records when you flipped weights?

alex_platform: authoritative TTL was 300s. I pushed weights 90/10 -> 0/100 at 1932104420. propagation is inconsistent across regions.

jin_sre: lowering TTL after the flip won't magically clear ISP caches. Some resolvers ignore low TTLs or clamp them. Steps we should do: 1) lower authoritative TTL to 30-60s, 2) bump SOA serial, 3) request CDN/edge purge if hostnames are cached on the edge. Also consider BGP steering if DNS convergence is slow.

sam_oncall: did TrafficManager health routing actually flip? logs show failover triggered but token logs say ~30% of traffic still landing in ap-southeast.

alex_platform: TrafficManager set to prefer us-east; healthchecks flipped. But regional NAT egress overlaps and some resolver caches are sticky. Quick dig from a few vantage points:

```
# office VPN
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.ai
203.0.113.12   ; ap-southeast

# home network
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai
198.51.100.9   ; us-east
```

maria_netops: paste the dig outputs (thanks). This matches: some public resolvers still returning old A records.

jin_sre: nailed it — resolver staleness. A few APAC ISPs are known to ignore short TTLs and clamp to a higher minimum. If TTL-based approach fails, we need to escalate to network steering: BGP more-specific announce or edge provider-level steering.

registrar_ops: I set authoritative TTL -> 60s at 1932104525 and incremented SOA serial. Also opened CDN purge for edge hostnames. Note: stubborn caches can still hold for a few minutes.

lina_prodsec: warning — shifting 100% to us-east may hit WAF per-IP rate limits. I'm temporarily raising per-IP thresholds for the failover window.

sam_oncall: scaling us-east replicas now: `kubectl scale deploy api --replicas=10 -n prod-us-east` — watching CPU/queues.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback completed for model-serving in ap-southeast at 1932104510.

alex_platform: telemetry: us-east latency improved, but ~12% of requests (from APAC resolver buckets) still returning errors because they hit the degraded region IP.

maria_netops: action items I kicked off: TTL authoritative -> 60 (done 1932104525); SOA bumped; CDN purge requested; opened a support ticket with major APAC ISP to ask about cache clamping; prepping a BGP fallback plan with traffic engineering.

jin_sre: runbook update suggestion: for planned maintenance, pre-lower TTL to 60s at least one TTL window before flip. Add automated detection: if >10% of requests still resolve to failing region 5 minutes after weight change, trigger BGP fallback playbook. Also, document that flipping TTLs during an active incident is often too late.

lina_prodsec: WAF thresholds relaxed by 60% for 20 minutes at 1932104550 :white_check_mark:.

sam_oncall: seeing resolver variance reduce after TTL change, but a subset of intermediate resolvers still return cached records per `dig +trace`. I estimate full convergence 10-15m for stubborn ASes.

alex_platform: post-incident TODOs: add pre-failover checklist (lower TTL before flip, confirm CDN/registrar purge path, notify prodsec to relax WAF, have BGP playbook ready), add auto-detect to trigger BGP if DNS convergence stalls, ask vendors for DNS weight-change abort/flush API.

maria_netops: creating the incident ticket and assigning owners now. Thanks for fast coordination everyone. :thumbsup:

jin_sre: post-incident follow-ups: schedule a tabletop to cover DNS failover + BGP interplay; we made some assumptions that need docs.

sam_oncall: will monitor for the next hour and close thread when error rate normalizes below SLO.

alex_platform: root cause: GPU pool exhaustion due to a CI regression that spawned runaway jobs. Follow-up with infra-cost/CI to add quota guardrails.

maria_netops: noted and creating follow-up tasks :eyes:
